response.text:
I can draft and send that, but a quick warning: committing to a hard date when you’re not sure internally can create problems if it slips. I recommend you confirm internally first — or send wording that sounds confident but leaves a small escape (e.g., “we will complete the migration on October 3” vs “we are on track to complete the migration on October 3”).

Below are two short drafts. Tell me which you want (firm vs. cautious), provide the client email address and the name/signature to use, and confirm you want me to send it.

Option A — Firm / Confident (commits to Oct 3)
Subject: Migration Completion Date — October 3
Hi [Client Name],
I’m writing to confirm that we will complete the migration on October 3. Our team is lined up and ready to execute the plan to ensure a smooth transition. I’ll follow up with final confirmation and any scheduling details next week. Please let me know if you have any questions.
Best regards,
[Your Name]

Option B — Confident but safer (less absolute)
Subject: Migration Target Date — October 3
Hi [Client Name],
We are on track to complete the migration by October 3. Our team is prepared and we’ll provide final confirmation and any scheduling details next week. Please let me know if you have any questions or timing constraints.
Best regards,
[Your Name]

What do you want me to do next? (Reply with: “Send A” or “Send B”, plus client email and the name/signature to use. I will not send until you confirm.)
